transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I came in today because I just feel like... I cannot settle inside my own skin anymore. 

I always feel like I have to jump up and do the next thing, even when I am completely worn out and I really should just be sitting still. It's just very hard for me to rest.
When did you first start noticing this difficulty with settling down and constantly needing to move to the next thing?
Well... I'd say it's been causing me real trouble since my husband died. That was about, oh, a year and 10 months ago now.
Besides this difficulty settling down and moving to the next thing, how has your mood been since your husband passed away? Have you been feeling sad, empty, or depressed?

Well, no, not really. I mean, naturally I miss him, but... I haven't been feeling empty or depressed, no. My mood is actually mostly okay. It's really just that restless feeling... like my motor just keeps running and I can't turn it off. But no, I wouldn't say I feel sad or down.

When you experience this restless feeling and need to keep moving, do you find yourself worrying about things or having anxious thoughts, or is it more just a physical restlessness without much worry on your mind?

Well, it's mostly just a physical thing. I don't really sit around worrying about a whole lot. My mind isn't racing with anxious thoughts or anything like that. It's just my body... I just can't seem to sit still. I don't feel nervous, just... restless.

When you're feeling this restless and your motor is running, do you notice your heart racing, sweating, or feeling tense in your muscles, or is it more like a mental agitation where you just feel compelled to do things?

No, I don't really get those physical things like a racing heart or sweating. My muscles don't feel tight or anything. It's really just... I just feel like I have to keep moving. Like you said, it's more that I just feel compelled to be doing something. I just can't settle.

Does this restless feeling and need to keep moving happen all the time, or do you notice it gets worse at certain times, like when you're thinking about your husband or doing things that remind you of him?

Well, no, it's not really tied to memories of him or anything like that. It's pretty much all the time. Most days I just go straight from working in the garden, to the senior center, to running church errands, and then back to sorting papers at home. I just keep going and going without taking a real breath. It's almost as if... well, like if I were to actually stop, everything would just fall apart.

Have you been having any unwanted thoughts about your husband's death that pop into your mind, or nightmares about it, or do you find yourself avoiding certain places or activities that remind you of him?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. I mean, I don't have nightmares about it, and bad thoughts don't just pop into my head out of nowhere. And I definitely don't avoid places that remind me of him... I actually like going to the places we used to go. So, no, I don't have those specific issues you're asking about.
You mentioned that if you stopped moving, everything would fall apart. Can you tell me more about what you mean by that? What do you think would happen if you actually sat still for a while?

Well, it's just that I can't seem to do the quiet things anymore. If I try to sit still... I don't know, it just doesn't work. Like, quiet things I used to enjoy, like sitting with a quilt pattern or reading my Bible, they don't stay quiet for long. I'll sit down, but then I start humming, or talking to myself, or I just end up getting up and fussing with something else. I just can't seem to stay put and focus on it.

When you're sitting still and trying to do something quiet like reading your Bible, and you start humming or talking to yourself instead, do you notice any uncomfortable feelings or emotions coming up that you're trying to get away from, or does it just feel like an urge to move without any particular feeling driving it?

I don't think it's really an uncomfortable feeling or anything I'm trying to run away from. It's more just... I don't know, it's just this urge to be doing something. It's not like I'm sitting there feeling sad or anxious and trying to distract myself. My body just wants to move, or I just need to make some noise or keep busy. I don't really feel anything specific driving it, it just happens.

Looking back over the past year and 10 months since your husband passed away, has this restless feeling and need to keep moving been getting any better, staying the same, or actually getting worse as time has gone on?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really noticed it changing one way or the other. It's hard to say if it's gotten better or worse... it just feels like it's always happening. I guess I haven't really kept track of it like that.

When you're doing all these activities—working in the garden, going to the senior center, sorting papers—do you feel like you're doing them because you genuinely want to or need to do them, or does it feel more like you're doing them to keep your mind off something or to avoid sitting alone with your thoughts?

I don't think I'm trying to avoid anything, really. I just... I do them because they're there to be done, I guess. Like the garden needs weeding, or the papers need sorting. I don't feel like I'm running away from my thoughts or trying to keep my mind off anything specific. It's just that I see something that needs doing, or I feel like I should be doing something, so I do it. I just like to stay busy.

Because of this constant need to keep moving and difficulty settling down, has it caused problems in your daily life—like difficulty sleeping, trouble concentrating, or affecting your ability to take care of things that matter to you?

Well, it has caused some real problems, yes. It's gotten to the point where my family has had to step in and take over my bills and paperwork because I just couldn't keep them straight. And... it's affecting other things, too. At church and at the community garden, people have had to redo plans or cover for me because I've dropped the ball on responsibilities I said I'd handle. It's really embarrassing, honestly. I just feel like these groups I care about... they don't feel like they can count on me anymore.

Have you had any recent medical illnesses, infections, or changes in your health around the time this restlessness started, or has your doctor mentioned anything about thyroid problems, hormone changes, or other medical conditions that might explain what you're experiencing?

No, not that I can think of. I haven't had any major illnesses or infections or anything like that. And my doctor hasn't said anything about my thyroid or hormones being off. Physically, I feel fine... well, besides the fact that I just can't seem to stop moving. But no, no new medical problems that I know of.

You mentioned this restlessness started about a year and 10 months ago, right around when your husband died. Did these feelings of needing to keep moving start right away after he passed, or did they develop gradually over weeks or months afterward?

Well, it started right away, really. Ever since he died—which was about a year and ten months ago—it's just been causing me all this real trouble. It wasn't something that crept up slowly over a few months or anything. It just... it started right then, and I haven't been able to settle down since.

opening_question.question: Hello, I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent psychomotor agitation and inability to settle since her husband's death 22 months ago. She denies depressed mood, anxious thoughts, intrusive memories, nightmares, or avoidance behaviors characteristic of PTSD. The restlessness is non-trauma-focused, lacks autonomic symptoms, and occurs without specific emotional triggers. Functional impairment is evident (family managing finances, dropped responsibilities). Medical causes have been ruled out. This presentation is consistent with Adjustment Disorder with Disturbance of Conduct and Emotions (F43.12), where the prominent feature is maladaptive behavioral response (constant activity, inability to focus on responsibilities) and emotional disturbance (restlessness, difficulty settling) in reaction to an identifiable stressor (spouse's death), with onset within 3 months and duration less than 6 months after stressor cessation would be expected.
